name: Machine Crunch
summary: A seated machine exercise that isolates the abdominal muscles by flexing the spine against guided resistance.

setup: Adjust the seat height so the machine's pivot point aligns with your lower ribs or mid-torso.
Select your desired resistance on the weight stack.
Sit back firmly against the back pad and secure your feet under the foot rollers or flat on the footrests.
Grasp the machine handles or rest your upper chest against the front pad according to the machine design.
steps: Contract your abdominal muscles to curl your ribcage down toward your pelvis.
Flex your spine forward in a controlled arc without pulling excessively with your arms or hip flexors.
Pause and squeeze your abdominals firmly at the point of maximum contraction.
Slowly reverse the movement under control, extending your spine until you return to the starting position without letting the weights slam.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you crunch your torso forward into full contraction, and inhale as you return to the upright position.
cues: Curl your ribs down to your hips
Squeeze your abs, don't yank with your arms
Control the stretch on the way up

common_faults.fault: Pulling primarily with the arms and shoulders rather than flexing the spine with the abdominals.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a light, steady grip on the handles and focus on drawing the ribcage down toward the pelvis.

common_faults.fault: Hinging entirely at the hips with a rigid, flat back.
common_faults.correction: Actively round your upper and mid-spine to flex the trunk and isolate the rectus abdominis.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the neck by tucking the chin excessively or throwing the head back.
common_faults.correction: Keep your neck in a neutral position relative to your thoracic spine throughout the movement.

precautions: Do not use excessive weight that forces you to brace through your hip flexors or compromise spine control.
